p: Roots of Unity was the capstone project for my NAIT Game Programming course. As students, our goal was to create a product for Room 322. We decided to accomplish this by creating a Bullet Heaven game called Roots of Unity.

My primary role was to ensure our version control was adequate for a project with 8 people pushing and pulling to GitHub at any given moment. I had spent the first leg of our project ensuring we had clear documentation that also helped the other students know the terminology of GitHub.

ul.li: Commit Often, and have each commit be roughly one fix, feature, change, etc. This allows for rollbacks of specific features without removing all of the other working code in one commit.

Pushes. If you find yourself finished the feature, ending your workday, or needing to share your work with someone else you will have to push your changes to the remote. This will confirm your changes as the truth. As you push GitHub Desktop will pull any changes just to make sure. This might run you into a merge conflict or you might be just fine.

Push On Unique Branches. All too often multiple people work on the same item in a branch and cause two versions of the same item. To help quell this problem, known as a Merge Conflict, you should change only new things in a separate new folder when altering a branch. We can format after merging said branch.

details.summary: Always have your commits be clear, concise, complete, and correct.

ul.li: Clear. To be clear means you are not obfuscating the information.
Concise. Your language should be short and read on a glance.
Complete. You shouldn't have incomplete sentences as your commit, . or a or thing or help me, etc, are not acceptable commits.
Correct. Your commit message should explain what the commit entails.
Always use GitMoji at the beginning of commit titles
development this branch is for all development to go into. It is set up as the default so when merging it will default to merge into this branch.
publishing this branch is exclusively for states of the game that are stable and playable. Make builds in this branch once you know the development branch is stable.

Branch Naming Conventions
feature/name for any new features.
bugfix/name for fixing some major bug.

ol.li: Work on Changes and Commit Regularly
If Feature is Done then open a Pull Request
Wait for Code Review & Approval before Merging

ul.li: When making a pull request always provide a descriptive title and summary of the changes.
You should never merge without having others check over the work.
To get people's attention you can add reviewers to check the request.
After it has been reviewed and confirmed then you can merge the changes. If everything was done correctly you should not get any merge conflicts.

details.p: You are required to fix the merge conflict before pushing your changes. Depending on what file is conflicted this might be incredibly easy or your worst nightmare.
.cs files should be very simple to fix. If it is a .meta or .unity file it may be impossible to fix.

ul.li:
Error Handling. When there might be an issue and incorrect data gets into a script you REQUIRE error handling. This includes standard things such as try { } catch { } or Guard Clauses.
No Commented Out Code. Once you are complete with an idea and it is working, remove commented out code if present.

Class Structure
One class per file. This can be different for maybe a general Interfaces.cs file but keep classes to one per file.
Standard Member Arrangement. Keep classes using this format.
Fields and Properties
Constructors (if any)
Unity Methods (e.g., Start, Update)
Custom Methods
Namespaces. With a large project such as this it is very useful to have namespaces such as namespace RootofUnity.Managers.
Access Modifiers. Always explicitly declare the access modifier you wish to use (public, private, internal, etc). Default should be private unless it requires broader access.
Regions. use #region as much as possible when grouping together information.
Classes & Interfaces Use PascalCase and add an additional I to the front of interfaces.
Methods, Enums, & Properties Use PascalCase.
Fieldsuse camelCase. (method variables fall under this aswell).
Constants use ALL_CAPS with an _ between words.
Private Variables add an _ before the variable.
